{{Other uses|Slew (disambiguation)}}
{{More citations needed|date=August 2026}}
'''Slewing''' is the [[rotation]] of an object around an axis, usually the [[z axis]].<ref name="mwcollegiate1993">{{Cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/merriamwebstersc0000unse_e5y1/page/1104/mode/1up?q=slew |title=Merriam-Webster's collegiate dictionary |date=1993 |publisher=Merriam-Webster |isbn=978-0-87779-708-1 |location=Springfield, Mass., U.S.A. |pages=1104}}</ref> An example is a [[radar]] scanning 360 degrees by slewing around the z axis. This is also common terminology in astronomy. The process of rotating a telescope to observe a different region of the sky is referred to as slewing.<ref name="hart-davis2007">{{Cite book |last=Hart-Davis |first=Adam |url=https://archive.org/details/cosmosbeginnersg0000hart/page/140/mode/2up |title=The cosmos: a beginner's guide |date=2007 |publisher=BBC Books |isbn=978-1-84607-212-3 |location=London |pages=140}}</ref>

The term slewing is also found in motion control applications.  Often the slew axis is combined with another axis to form a motion profile.

In [[Crane (machine)|crane]] terminology, slewing is the angular movement of a crane boom or crane jib in a horizontal plane.

The term is also used in the [[computer game]] [[Microsoft Flight Simulator]] wherein the user presses a key and they can rotate and move the virtual aircraft along all [[Three-dimensional space|three spatial planes]].

In the modern day use of CNC programs, ''slewing'' is a vital part of the process.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}
